overview: The Community Preservation Committee voted to recommend funding for emergency repairs to the Royall House perimeter wall and reviewed a small grant request for the Osgood House. The committee also received informational updates on the Affordable Housing Trust and the Walkling Court redevelopment.

items.title: Osgood House Gutter Restoration Small Grant Application
items.summary: The committee reviewed an $11,000 small grant request from the Unitarian Universalist Church to repair gutters and molding at the historic Osgood House, continuing the item to next month so the applicant can explore material options compliant with historic preservation standards and within the $10,000 program cap.

items.title: Royall House Perimeter Wall Emergency Restoration
items.summary: Recommended approval of an emergency off-cycle grant request to repair a bowing section of the historic brick perimeter wall at the Royall House and Slave Quarters, conditioned on administrative review of lead flashing material safety and project approval by the Massachusetts Historical Commission.

items.title: Affordable Housing Trust Fund Update
items.summary: Representatives from the Affordable Housing Trust presented an update on their strategic action plan, board finances, and funding support for Medford Community Housing's three-unit development at 703 Fellsway West.

items.title: Walkling Court Redevelopment Update
items.summary: Medford Housing Authority representatives provided an update on the Walkling Court redevelopment, reporting that a guaranteed maximum price contract was finalized with Consigli and Phase 1 construction is scheduled to begin in late summer 2026.

items.title: Administrator's Update
items.summary: Staff reviewed upcoming community tabling events for public outreach and noted planning for the committee's August social outing.
